document_check.note: The document is Amland R, Selbaek G, Braekhus A, Edwin TH, Engedal K, Knapskog AB, Olsrud ER, Persson K, 'Clinically feasible automated MRI volumetry of the brain as a prognostic marker in subjective and mild cognitive impairment', Frontiers in Neurology 15:1425502 (2024), doi:10.3389/fneur.2024.1425502. Prospective memory-clinic cohort (Oslo University Hospital), 156 patients with SCD or MCI and a follow-up visit, NeuroQuant hippocampus percentile and whole-brain volume as prognostic factors for conversion and for annual CDR-SB change (Tables 2 to 9, pp. 6-9).

cited_result: Hippocampus volume percentile as a prognostic factor for conversion from subjective or mild cognitive impairment to a more impaired stage, in the 141 patients with complete data: OR 0.98 (p = 0.002) unadjusted, OR 0.98 (p = 0.028) adjusted for age, sex and follow-up time (model 1), and OR 0.99 (p = 0.060) once the MMSE-NR score was added (model 2; Table 2, p. 6); in the 120-patient subsample with APOE status the model-2 association remained (OR 0.98, p = 0.025; Table 6, p. 8). Hippocampus percentile and whole-brain volume were both associated with the annual change in CDR-SB in unadjusted and adjusted models (Tables 4 and 5, pp. 7-8).
tool_reason: The cited result is the association of a single baseline measure (hippocampus volume percentile) with a later outcome, estimated with adjustment rather than as a multivariable prediction model, so QUIPS applies (six domains).

domains.rationale: The source population and setting are described, but the analysed patients are a minority of those seen: only patients referred for NeuroQuant MRI were eligible (most memory-clinic patients had already been scanned elsewhere), and 156 of 297 eligible patients had a follow-up visit. The followed-up and not-followed-up groups did not differ on the baseline variables compared.

signalling.question: Is the source population and sampling frame adequately described?
signalling.quote: A total of 297 patients examined at the memory clinic at OUH between 2010 and 2020, diagnosed with SCD (n = 99) or MCI (n = 198), who had been examined with MRI of the brain including assessment with NQ, were eligible for inclusion.

signalling.question: Is the baseline sample representative of the source population?
signalling.quote: The only reason for not referring a patient to this assessment was if MRI was contraindicated or if the patient had already been examined with MRI previous to the referral to the memory clinic (this was the case in 80% of the patients being examined at the memory clinic).

signalling.question: Is the proportion participating and their characteristics reported?
signalling.quote: Of the 297 patients, 156 (46 diagnosed with SCD and 110 diagnosed with MCI at baseline) had at least one clinical follow-up examination and were included in this prospective longitudinal study. | Analyses comparing patients who were followed up (n = 156) with those who were not (n = 141) showed no significant difference in age (p 0.398), sex (p 0.688), education (p 0.271), CDR-SB scores (p 0.196) or the Mini-Mental State Examination-Norwegian Revision (MMSE-NR) scores (p 0.055).

domains.rationale: Follow-up length varied from 7 to 91 months and the last visit was used; 141 of 156 had complete data for the logistic models and 117 for the linear models, with no imputation and no comparison of those with incomplete data.

signalling.question: Is the proportion lost to follow-up and the reasons reported?
signalling.quote: Overall, 141 patients, were not followed up, possibly due to a lack of clinical indication for additional evaluation or because patients declined any follow-up consultations (see Figure 1 for details).

signalling.question: Are those with complete data comparable to those without?
signalling.quote: Only patients with complete data were included in the regression analyses, i.e., 141 in the logistic regression models and 117 in the linear regression models.

signalling.question: Was follow-up long and uniform enough for the outcome?
signalling.quote: If a patient had multiple follow-up consultations the last visit was registered and utilized to evaluate longitudinal progression. The mean follow-up time was 32.6 months (range: 7-91 months).

domains.rationale: The prognostic factor is an FDA-approved automated volumetric output (hippocampus percentile, age- and sex-adjusted against normative data) measured the same way for all patients; software versions and a scanner upgrade were recorded and adjusted for where associated with the outcome.

signalling.question: Is a clear definition of the prognostic factor provided (including cut-points)?
signalling.quote: First, the clinically applicable hippocampus percentile because hippocampus atrophy is known to be strongly associated with AD (16, 17). All hippocampus percentile calculations were based on NQ version 1 and 2.

signalling.question: Was the factor measured similarly and validly for all participants?
signalling.quote: T1-weighted 3D scanning was performed on a 3 Tesla MRI scanner (GE Signa HDxt) that was upgraded to GE Discovery MR750 in 2015. All of the included patients were scanned with a study specific protocol, including similar 3D T1-w gradient echo sequence.

signalling.question: Were measurement differences handled?
signalling.quote: Age, sex, and MMSE-NR were included as covariates in all models while education, follow-up time, MRI scanner, and NQ version were only adjusted for if the association to the dependent variable was p < 0.2.

domains.rationale: Conversion was diagnosed retrospectively from records by one of three clinician-researchers using research criteria, with senior review of inconclusive cases, but without blinding to the MRI (which was part of the clinical work-up) and with some records incomplete; CDR-SB was scored from records and could not be computed for 25 patients.

signalling.question: Is a clear definition of the outcome provided?
signalling.quote: Converters were defined as patients who progressed to a more impaired level of cognitive functioning-that is, from SCD at baseline to MCI or dementia at follow-up, or from MCI at baseline to dementia at follow-up.

signalling.question: Was the outcome measured validly, reliably and blind to the prognostic factor?
signalling.quote: Diagnoses were made retrospectively based on all available information from the examinations at baseline and at follow-up. | Because the diagnoses were made post hoc based on patient records, we cannot rule out that some details may have been missing in the reports and could have affected the diagnostic evaluation.

signalling.question: Was the outcome measured similarly for all?
signalling.quote: The CDR was scored by one of three CDR-certified researchers (i.e., T.H.E., K.P., or R.A.) based on the available information from the patients' records, including information from an interview with the caregiver. The CDR was scored by the same researcher at baseline and follow-up.

domains.rationale: Age, sex, follow-up time and baseline MMSE were adjusted for in all models, and APOE in a subsample; baseline diagnosis (SCD against MCI), amyloid status and vascular burden were not, and covariate selection used a p < 0.2 screen.

signalling.question: Are all important confounders measured?
signalling.quote: Specific AD biomarkers from cerebrospinal fluid or amyloid positron emission tomography were not included in the diagnostic evaluation as these examinations were only performed on clinical indication and were only available in 64 of the included patients.

signalling.question: Are confounders accounted for in the analysis?
signalling.quote: in model 1, we adjusted for age, sex, and follow-up time, and in model 2, we additionally adjusted for MMSE-NR score at baseline to adjust for cognitive stage.

signalling.question: Is the handling of confounding appropriate?
signalling.quote: Lastly, in a subgroup of patients with available APOE e4 carrier status, we repeated the analyses on conversion (n = 120) and progression (n = 100) by adjusting for the same variables as in the previous regression analyses with the addition of APOE e4 carrier status.

domains.rationale: Logistic and linear regression are appropriate for the design, and the models are reported in full, but there are 38 converters for up to seven covariates, the covariate set was chosen by a p < 0.2 screen, several overlapping models are reported and the model-2 result the review relies on is a change from p = 0.028 to p = 0.060 with the odds ratio unchanged to two decimals.

signalling.question: Is the statistical model appropriate for the design?
signalling.quote: First, logistic regression was used to explore the predictive properties of hippocampus percentile and WBV on conversion to MCI or dementia. | Secondly, multiple linear regression analyses were performed to explore the predictive properties of the hippocampus percentile and WBV on the progression of cognitive and functional decline, measured as the annual change in CDR-SB score.

signalling.question: Are the number of events adequate for the model?
signalling.quote: Of the 38 converters 7 converted from SCD to MCI, 3 from SCD to dementia, and 28 converted from MCI to dementia during the follow-up-time (Figure 1).

signalling.question: Is there selective reporting?
signalling.quote: In model 2, which included MMSE-NR as a covariate, the association was no longer significant (OR 0.99, p 0.060), see Table 2. | Analyses in the subsample with available APOE e4 results (n = 120), including APOE e4 status as a covariate, showed an association between hippocampus percentile and conversion in both models 1 and 2

signalling.question: Were the results reported with precision?

overall: High risk of bias (QUIPS, by this review's rule: four domains moderate, one low, none high)
overall_rationale: No domain is high, but participation, attrition, outcome measurement, confounding and analysis are each moderate, which under this review's QUIPS rule (three or more moderate domains) gives an overall high risk. The specific result the review cites, the loss of significance once baseline MMSE is adjusted for, is a borderline change (OR 0.98 to 0.99, p 0.028 to 0.060) in a model with 38 events, and the same association remained significant in the APOE subsample; it supports 'cognitive stage absorbs part of the hippocampal signal' and not 'hippocampal volume carries no information beyond the MMSE'.

applicability.rationale: Memory-clinic patients with SCD or MCI referred for NeuroQuant MRI in one hospital; younger (mean 63 to 70 years) and more educated than many clinic cohorts.
A clinically available automated hippocampal volume output, the measure the review's comparison concerns.
Conversion to a more impaired stage from a mixed SCD and MCI baseline, not MCI-to-dementia conversion alone.
